exercises.answer_key: This question rounds "the numbers in question 3", printed on the PRECEDING page (printed 18, pg_018.json — now captured and present in this corpus). Q3 on printed 18 was 'Which numbers do these arrows show?' with 4 arrows on a 30-80 number line, answered (measured twice, two independent pixel methods, both agreed): arrow a=38, b=55, c=62, d=79. Rounded to the nearest 10: a. 38 -> 40; b. 55 -> 60 (round-half-up convention, standard in this curriculum); c. 62 -> 60; d. 79 -> 80.
exercises.answer_confidence: medium (arithmetic itself is certain; confidence is medium only on whether this page's a/b/c/d order matches printed-18 Q3's arrow 1-4 left-to-right order, which is the natural reading — the blanks themselves are unlabelled fill-in lines with no numbers printed on this page)

exercises.label: Adventure Begins! — Guess the stall by ordinal position
exercises.instruction_verbatim: I'll describe stall items, and you have to guess which stall number (ordinal position) it belongs to. 1. Which stall has colourful clothes hanging beautifully? 2. Which stall has a ring toss game set up? 3. Which stall has Jalebis?
items: 2nd stall: a bowl of food (biryani/rice dish with a chicken drumstick)
3rd stall: a ring-toss game (yellow peg with coloured rings)
6th stall: a glass jar of green pickles (achaar)
7th stall: a mehndi/henna cone on a stick
8th stall: a folded green checkered cloth/notebook
9th stall: a stack of black-and-white patterned bangles
exercises.answer_key: 1. 4th stall (the red-and-blue shirt). 2. 3rd stall (the ring-toss game). 3. 10th stall (the jalebis).
